common_name: Pink Cupid Pacific Coast Iris (Sydney B. Mitchell Medal Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall into humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade; Pacific Coast Iris resents root disturbance, so divide only when truly necessary.

directions: Plant in full sun to light shade in humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil; Pink Cupid, bred by Vernon Wood, won the American Iris Society's Sydney B. Mitchell Medal in 2000, the top award for Pacific Coast Native iris hybrids. Like other Pacific Coast irises it forms an evergreen, grassy-leaved clump and blooms in spring, thriving in the mild, dry-summer Mediterranean climate typical of its native California and Oregon range. It resents transplanting and root disturbance once established, so site it in a permanent spot with excellent drainage.
sources: American Iris Society
Society for Pacific Coast Native Iris
